rationale: This is a mechanical recombination of two archive signals (the EBITDA-growth leg of "Debt-Funded EBITDA Improvement" times the negated change-in-net-liquid-assets leg of "Net-Liquid Profitability"), and because the rank leg is confined to [0,1] the signal's sign is entirely driven by the already-tested liquidity leg, so it largely re-runs the prior result with the sign flipped.

It reuses the same two ingredients as the archive's "Cash-Share-Verified Core Margin" but substituting persistent 3-period trends for a level and a one-period change is a defensible, motivated response to that signal's weak portfolio tails rather than a pure relabeling — though it remains a modest refinement rather than a new mechanism.

The expression correctly implements the stated realization cycle (prior-year working-capital build, current-year release, conditioned on profitability), the timing structure is genuinely distinct from the standard accruals level/change anomaly, and the profitability gate plausibly separates harvesting from distress-driven liquidation; the main risk is that a three-way MIN gate yields thin, unstable long tails.

The construction is internally consistent and the depreciation-quality channel is under-explored relative to accrual signals, but because Δ(oiadp/sale) mechanically contains −Δ(dpc/sale), the two legs are algebraically overlapping and any result will be hard to distinguish from a plain depreciation-intensity-change signal (itself close to the Abarbanell–Bushee fundamental signals).

With the profit-growth leg bounded in [0,1], the signal reduces to a positively-weighted receivables-accrual measure whose predicted negative sign is simply the Sloan/receivables accrual anomaly, and the label "conditional" misdescribes what is a signed multiplicative product with no gate.

A three-way MIN gate on profitability, R&D intensity, and an archive cash-share change leg is a kitchen-sink composite whose R&D-plus-profitability core rediscovers the established R&D-intensity/quality anomaly, while the economic link between R&D expensing and a one-year cash-share shift is asserted rather than argued, and the conjunction of high profitability with high R&D will leave a narrow, sector-concentrated long tail.
